lead.headline: AI proves a 2011 quantum computing conjecture
signal: Lean-style verification is what lets AI proofs be trusted; fields without a verifier will move slower.
lead.hook: Researchers used Anthropic's Fable 5.2 model to prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, which says quantum computers cannot beat ordinary ones on a class of random-input problems; the model took about four days.
points: The conjecture was set by Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis in 2011. Ambainis says he had given up on it.
David Turturean of start-up Physical Superintelligence led the team. The model refined the proof twice, then Lean proof-checking software verified it.
Stanford researchers studied it and call it substantially more difficult than prior work, woven together in a novel way.
It rules out one place to look for quantum speed-ups, but Aaronson says it was not a plausible direction anyway.
Quantum advantage may remain for shorter or less random inputs, molecule simulation and some optimisation problems.
lead.evidence_of: AI is now solving research-level maths problems

stories.headline: FDA's 2026 warning letters hit Asia hard, BioSpectrum finds
signal: Public letters within days mean quality gaps become headlines before firms can respond; Indian exporters need records ready.
stories.hook: The US FDA posted 513 warning letters between 13 January and 10 November 2026; 59 went to Asia-Pacific firms, 25 to India and 22 to China.
points: Of 121 letters on drug manufacturing quality, 45 went to sites in the region.
The median drug quality letter appeared on fda.gov eight days after it was issued, often before the company's reply was due.
FDA enforced in coordinated waves, such as compounded GLP-1 marketing and talc products, and import alerts often come before the letter.
BioSpectrum's whitepaper covers cases including Reliance Life Sciences, Eugia, Intas, Zydus and Dabur.

also.line: STAT's health-tech newsletter reports new documents raising more questions about Medicare's AI prior-authorization experiment (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: India funds deeptech, but who will buy what it builds?
signal: Without government purchase commitments, funded startups may lack first customers.
stories.hook: Agnikul Cosmos received Rs 200 crore from the RDI Fund to build a reusable launch vehicle, but The CapTable says the government has no matching buyer (summary from limited source text).
points: The Government of India has built a large pipeline of deeptech funding.
The missing piece is demand inside the system for the technology being funded.

stories.headline: Ukrainian defence startup UFORCE ==raised $700M== at a $6B valuation
signal: If bookings growth holds, the valuation rests on proven combat use; customers remain undisclosed.
stories.hook: UFORCE raised $700 million at a $6 billion valuation, up from about $1 billion in March when it raised $50 million.
points: Valor Equity Partners and the UK's National Wealth Fund co-led the Series A.
The CEO says bookings more than doubled in a year from a base of several hundred million dollars; he gave no exact figures.
It makes unmanned air, sea and land systems plus AI to coordinate them; it says NEMESIS drones have flown over 300,000 combat flights.
Funds will scale manufacturing in Ukraine and allied countries; the CEO says Ukrainian needs come first.
Startups across NATO and allied countries raised $27.1 billion through September, nearly double all of 2025.
stories.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

stories.headline: Moody's: no clear sign yet of AI hitting Indian IT jobs
signal: Absence of evidence now doesn't mean none later; compute and skills are the constraints to watch.
stories.hook: Moody's says AI's impact on jobs and productivity is not yet clearly visible in India, even though India and the Philippines are the emerging markets most exposed through IT and BPO.
points: AI could both raise productivity and displace jobs in software, IT and BPO-heavy economies.
Access to computing power, digital infrastructure and skilled workers will decide how much countries gain.
Moody's raised India's FY27 GDP growth __forecast to 7% from 6.5%__.
For China and India, higher interest payments are expected to add more to public debt than budget deficits.
Its sovereign outlook lists weaker-than-expected AI investment returns as a key risk.
stories.evidence_of: AI lets firms grow revenue with fewer hires

patterns.name: AI is now solving research-level maths problems
patterns.line: An AI model proved a 2011 quantum-computing conjecture in about four days, and Scientific American reports AI moving from maths towards physics. Maths has proof checkers; most sciences lack them, which limits the spread.

evidence.title: AI confirms a long-suspected limit on quantum computers’ advantages

patterns.name: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons
patterns.line: Ukraine launched nearly 1,200 drones in one night, India's Army plans 540 jet-powered kamikaze drones, and UFORCE raised $700M at a $6B valuation. Battlefield results are pulling in both procurement and private money.

evidence.title: Ukrainian defense tech startup hits $6 billion valuation as investors bet on battle-tested drones
